SOURCE III — FULL COUPERIN PERFORMANCE AND ELECTRONIC REVOICING

Human performance
François Couperin — L’Art de toucher le clavecin (complete musical pieces).
Harpsichord: David Joseph Stith, Gerald Self instrument built in 2020.
Recorded 27 January 2021. The performer-uploaded primary page describes a
TASCAM DR-100MKIII recording, processed with sox treble -4/bass +11.

Primary source:
https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Fran%C3%A7ois_Couperin_%22L%27Art_de_toucher_le_Clavecin%22.wav

The uploader dedicates this recording to the public domain under CC0 1.0:
https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/

Downloaded Commons MP3 transcode: 23,385,412 bytes; 843.157120 seconds.
SHA256: f9a9f0cefd38a4b7742f25e7636f88830b8a8ceed41167da7193426d0f80ae3a

The existing 11-second sheet excerpt is strongly correlated with this same
human take: its interior 1–9 seconds matches full 308.7105–316.7105 seconds,
normalized waveform correlation 0.985842. This does not imply encoded byte
identity. The full Source III performance does not repeat that short excerpt.

Prepared carrier
public/audio/source-rest/couperin/couperin-revoiced-pair.mp3
20,238,381 bytes; 32 kHz stereo; 192 kbps; decoded duration 843.157125 seconds.
SHA256: d2e43c31c04d69572cf70222fdfc63056b87081b6f218426a756c5ba085d97e9
Channel 0: mono downmix of the complete credited human performance.
Channel 1: newly synthesized electronic revoicing, not a second performer.
Both channels share one sample clock and one encoded decoder delay. In game,
they are blended as stems into the same room; they are not a left/right mix.

The generator infers 9,153 polyphonic note candidates using Spotify Basic Pitch
ICASSP 2022 ONNX (Apache 2.0 analysis dependency; existing isolated CPU runtime).
No model or inference engine ships in game. Additive/FM bass, struck middle
and glass upper voices follow inferred actual onsets, durations and register.
The electronic stem contains no copied source waveform. The preparation adds
no tempo quantization, score-based pitch correction or artificial error
stingers. Performed timing and irregularities remain; this does not certify
which sounds are performer mistakes. Automatic transcription may introduce
omissions, octave/partial errors and split/merged notes or ornaments.

Manifest and reproducible generator:
public/audio/source-rest/couperin/couperin-revoicing.json
tools/chunk_surfer/build-source-rest-couperin.py

The full source, prepared carrier and model hashes, timing/confidence method,
decoded headroom and limitations are retained in the manifest. A +6.0944 cent
fine-tuning estimate aligns synthesized pitches with the recording; it is not
a historical-temperament reconstruction. The decoded dry equal-power bound
is 0.310724 peak, with 0 clipped and 0 nonfinite samples. Native mix and musician
acceptance remain separate validation.

Credit and identity
The game credits David Joseph Stith for this human harpsichord performance,
and identifies the performance-derived electronic revoicing made for Chunk
Surfer. It does not attribute this harpsichord performance to the player or
developer. Source II’s Bach Chaconne is the separate developer-supplied
marimba recording. No third-party rights claim for Couperin extends to that
personal recording, and no claim is made that an autobiographical electronic
recording already existed. The new revoicing was created for this game.
